CLINICAL DOCUMENTATION — NARRATIVE INPATIENT DISCHARGE SUMMARY V1
Patient: Robert Smith | MRN: PAT-60003 | DOB: 1958-08-23 | Gender: Male | Doc ID: NARRATIVE_0003
Encounter Date: 2025-02-17 | Discharge/Note Date: 2025-02-19 | Provider: Dr. Sarah Jenkins, MD
CHIEF COMPLAINT
The patient presented with generalized fatigue, productive cough, and persistent fevers.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
The patient is a 49-year-old male with a medical history pertinent for hypertension and dyslipidemia who presented for
evaluation of generalized fatigue, productive cough, and persistent fevers. Symptoms began approximately four days prior
to admission and escalated in severity. On presentation to the emergency department, initial diagnostic evaluation
demonstrated that potassium was 4.61 mmol/L. Concurrently, serum chemistry was notable for a white blood cell count of
7.2 10*3/uL. Vital signs upon arrival were stable, and the patient was admitted to the inpatient general medicine service.
HOSPITAL COURSE
During the hospital course, the inpatient team initiated targeted management. The patient received Lisinopril 40 mg by
mouth every morning with good clinical tolerance. Serial assessments revealed gradual resolution of presenting symptoms.
Prior to planned discharge, repeat laboratory testing confirmed that calcium stabilized at 12.4 mg/dL (HIGH). The patient
was ambulating without assistance and tolerating a regular diet.
DISCHARGE MEDICATIONS
The patient was discharged home in stable clinical condition with instructions to take Metformin 1000 mg oral BID, and
Omeprazole 20 mg by mouth once daily in the morning. Medication reconciliation was completed and all questions
regarding dosing schedules were answered.
DISCHARGE INSTRUCTIONS & FOLLOW-UP
The patient was advised to follow up with their primary care physician within 7 to 10 days. Return precautions for chest pain,
recurrent shortness of breath, or fever were provided and understood.
